$meta.purpose: Index of the PDF shelf (PDFs are gitignored; this file is the tracked record). Shelf-first rule: grep THIS FILE and the *_taxonomy.json owned_regions before any web search or 'new lead' claim.

fields.summary_basis: read = primary source read in the programme (see read_trail); abstract = first page/abstract only; memory = from title + standard knowledge, UNVERIFIED
fields.verdict_for_us: owns (owns a region we touch; see programme_links) / neighbour / lens / unread
fields.read_trail: non-archive repo files mentioning the file stem or first-author surname (auto; surname matches can be noisy)

$meta.maintenance: Every PDF saved to the shelf gets an entry in the same commit. Seed tool: notes/literature_review/tools/shelf_index_seed.py.

questions.additivity_of_sums: Does E[f]+E[g] = E[f+g] when f, g are not jointly measurable (Gudder's problem)? Programme: impossible points, case 4 core Z1.
questions.impossible_point: Can askable questions expose a state concentrated at an impossible triple? (gate.triangle_density_plus1)
questions.clock_holonomy: Synchronisation round a loop; Sagnac; case 4.
questions.asynchrony: Observers without a shared clock (definitions_draft section 12).
questions.contextuality_finite: Finite, probabilistic local-vs-global (owned by contextuality theory).
questions.loop_count_witnesses: Hidden-twist witnesses = loop counts / n-cycle facets.
questions.marginal_problem: Existence of a joint with prescribed marginals (Vorob'ev, Kellerer, Maharam).
questions.coherence_extension: Extending coherent states from a carrier to all events.
questions.finitely_additive_charges: Charges, de Finetti coherence, imprecise probability.
questions.carriers_logics: Concrete logics / sigma-classes / partial Boolean algebras as 'the questions you can ask'.
questions.carrier_membership: Proving a set is NOT buildable (Dynkin non-membership).
questions.sigma_essential_background: Set-theoretic topology and measure background for the sigma-essential thread.
questions.data_tests: Testing real data for joint existence.
questions.completeness_points: Completeness theorems; when coherent = has a point.
questions.idealisation: Idealisations in physics (real numbers, infinite populations).
questions.philosophy_perspectives: Perspectives, relational facts, relations vs relata (structural realism, perspectival realism, RQM, Wigner's friend).

entries.citation: Abramsky & Barbosa, 'The logic of contextuality', CSL 2021, LIPIcs 183, arXiv:2011.03064
entries.what_it_proves: Partial Boolean algebras; logical exclusivity principle; Specker's principle (pairwise compatibility implies global); the triangle is its failure.

entries.citation: Abramsky & Barbosa, 'Duality for partial Boolean algebras', Topos Institute colloquium slides, 2025
entries.what_it_proves: Stone-type duality for partial Boolean algebras (Kochen-Specker's algebras of jointly observable properties).

entries.citation: Abramsky, Barbosa, Kishida, Lal, Mansfield, 'Possibilities determine the combinatorial structure of probability polytopes', J. Math. Psych. 2016, arXiv:1603.07735
entries.what_it_proves: Face lattice of the no-signalling polytope = support lattice; vertices = local deterministic + minimal-support strongly contextual (Prop 6.3).

entries.citation: Abramsky & Brandenburger, 'The sheaf-theoretic structure of non-locality and contextuality', New J. Phys. 13 (2011) 113036
entries.what_it_proves: Thm 8.1: factorizable hidden-variable realization iff global section; Thm 5.9: realization with negative probabilities iff no-signalling (signed extension automatic, cf. Maharam, Kellerer); Prop 5.8.
entries.read_note: targeted reading pass 2026-10-20 (theorem pages; see entry text for unread parts)

entries.citation: Abramsky, Barbosa, Kishida, Lal, Mansfield, 'Contextuality, cohomology and paradox', CSL 2015, arXiv:1502.03097
entries.what_it_proves: Logical paradoxes (e.g. liar cycles) and contextuality as cohomological obstructions to global sections.

entries.citation: Abramsky, Mansfield, Barbosa, 'The cohomology of non-locality and contextuality', QPL 2011, EPTCS 95, arXiv:1111.3620
entries.what_it_proves: Cech cohomology obstructions to global sections for empirical models; cover-dependence of the obstruction.

entries.citation: Adlam & Rovelli, 'Information is physical: cross-perspective links in relational quantum mechanics', Phil. Phys. 1(1) (2023), arXiv:2203.13342
entries.what_it_proves: Adds a 'cross-perspective links' postulate to RQM so that perspectives agree when compared; imposes consistency rather than diagnosing where inconsistency shows.

entries.citation: Amemiya & Araki, 'A remark on Piron's paper', Publ. RIMS 2 (1966)
entries.what_it_proves: Subspace lattice of a pre-Hilbert space is orthomodular iff the space is complete.

entries.citation: Biesel, 'Sheaves of probability', arXiv:2401.01968 (2024)
entries.what_it_proves: Thm 4/11 (p.3): pairwise agreement (generalized conditionalization) + a common positive event => unique global P on the union of evidence sets; Ex 3: triangle of agents pairwise compatible, no global P (logically inconsistent); Thm 8: probability is a sheaf for FINITE covers, countable covers fail (Remark 7). Covers by events, not sub-algebras.

entries.citation: Goodrick, 'Amalgamation properties for types in stable theories and beyond', BIRS workshop 09w5113 slides (2009)
entries.what_it_proves: 3-amalgamation problem for complete types p12, p23, p13; coherence (agreement on single variables) necessary; counterexamples: linear order x1<x2<x3<x1, and an equivalence relation with two classes with not-E in every p_ij; stable theories have 3-existence; o-minimal cannot (order cycle).

entries.citation: Goodrick, Kim, Kolesnikov, 'Amalgamation functors and boundary properties in simple theories', Israel J. Math. (2013), arXiv:1006.4410
entries.what_it_proves: n-amalgamation functors over INDEPENDENT problems; 3-existence holds in all simple theories (p.1, verified); boundary groups Aut(ab~/a b) profinite abelian (Thm 2.18); obstructions start at 4-existence / 3-uniqueness.

entries.citation: Goodrick, Kim, Kolesnikov, 'Type-amalgamation properties and polygroupoids in stable theories', J. Math. Logic (2015), arXiv:1404.1525

entries.citation: Goodrick, Kim, Kolesnikov, 'Homology groups of types in stable theories and the Hurewicz correspondence', APAL (2017), arXiv:1412.3864

entries.citation: Hrushovski, 'Stable group theory and approximate subgroups', JAMS 25 (2012) 189-243, arXiv:0909.2190
entries.what_it_proves: Remark 2.19(3) (verified): with a definable equivalence relation with boundedly many classes, 3-amalgamation of types can fail ('cannot amalgamate p(x,y) implying not xEy with types implying xEy, yEz'); 'it is possible that this is the only obstruction'. Section 2.20 (verified): a triangle of 2-types need not give a 3-type (definable linear order x<y, y<z, z<x), 'but in a measured setting ... this obstruction has effect only on a measure zero set' (Lemma 2.21, definable commuting measures).

entries.citation: Keleti & Preiss, 'The balls do not generate all Borel sets using complements and countable disjoint unions', Math. Proc. Camb. Phil. Soc. 128 (2000) 539-547

Template for non-membership: crossing + absorbing sigma-ideal + perturbation stability. Built on countable unions and a topological ideal: lens only for discrete Z^3.

entries.what_it_proves: Two-valued m: additivity of int(f+g) iff m concentrated on C_{f,g}; holds if R_f nowhere dense, R_g != R, one bounded on one side; K(a,b) sets with 1_K = 1{f<a}+1{g<b}-1{f+g<a+b}; final non-two-valued example on Z x N_0.

entries.citation: Navara, 'Integration on generalized measure spaces', Acta Univ. Carolinae Math. Phys. 30 (1989) 121-124
entries.what_it_proves: Thm 1 (pp.122-3): f bounded with nowhere dense range, closure of range g bounded countable => additive (open: drop countability). Thm 2 (p.123): m a countable convex combination of states two-valued on B_f, B_g; (1) f or g bounded on one side, (2) closure H of {(f,g)} nowhere dense, (3) R^2 minus H connected => additive. Remark 3: P x Q example (P = 2^Z, Q rationals) with int f = 2, int g = 0, int(f+g) = 1 shows (3) needed. Z^2: (2),(3) hold, (1) fails (cf. D-S Ex 6). Open: extension of m to the sigma-algebra.
